initial.claim: For every positive-characteristic ACFH model, inverse Frobenius is a parameter-free definable multiplicative automorphism outside Z[theta]. Adjoining it to the integral polynomial subring gives a faithfully embedded Z[1/p][X].
initial.proof: Use algebraically independent t_i in the algebraic closure of the rational extension. The old multiplicative group together with the needed t_i is the direct product, so the homomorphism extending theta and sending successive t_i to t_{i+1} is well-defined. A divisible codomain permits extension to the whole multiplicative group; define the field operator at zero separately. Transfer nontrivial Laurent monomial via an existential formula after clearing negative powers. [p] is nonzero central Frobenius, inverse has y^p=x graph, and pP-1 cannot vanish in Z[X]; invertibility and faithfulness give localization.

math: Extend the operator to an algebraic closure containing independent indeterminates, matching successive iterates by extending a partial homomorphism with divisible codomain. Existential closure supplies a nonzero value for every nonzero integral polynomial by clearing negative powers without adding language symbols. Frobenius scalar [p] is an invertible central group map and is not ring zero. Its inverse is parameter-free definable by y^p=x and cannot be a polynomial in θ since pP−1 cannot vanish. Adjoining it embeds the central localization, with injectivity by clearing p.

adversary.finding: Independently used roots of unity of arbitrary order prime to p in an ACFH model with θ initially the identity to disprove the universal equality, separate from the stronger all-positive-model proof. Checked full group/torsion, characteristic, and language scope.
